summary: [spec fidelity + standards] Two hints that start with `canon ` are prose, which brief F4 and Acceptance F4 forbid (7.1.2): `canon brief --json` and `canon report --json` (COMMAND_REQUIRED, exit 2) print hint `canon brief without a subcommand was removed in 0.28.0; use `canon brief show` (a group is never runnable; ...)` and the same for `report`. Removed::hint() (removed.rs:68) builds them with format!("{} was removed ...", self.used) where `used` is `canon <group> without a subcommand` (removed.rs:304). The test atip_contract11_10 cannot see them: source_hints() reads only the first string literal of a `.hint(...)` call and `*HINT*` consts, so a hint built from a runtime value is never scanned, and the frozen corpus has no bare-group case. I found them by running every leaf with --bogus, --input '{', '[1]', extra operands, and each group bare, then splitting every hint that starts with `canon`: 4 hints did, 2 are prose (these), 2 are `canon schema --errors|--warnings --json`. Proposed fix: make the bare-group hint start with something that is not `canon` (e.g. `a group is never runnable: use `canon brief show`...`) or just `canon brief show`; and add a test that runs each group bare (and each removed row) through the binary and applies problem() to the printed hint. Blast radius: every Removed row whose `used` starts with `canon` (only the bare-group rows today) and any future computed hint, none of which the scan exercises.
